first_impression.reaction: The title made me roll my eyes a bit ('You Did Not Know?' is clickbait), but the opening is sensible. Splitting the church service from the family folklore is exactly the kind of thing that stops us looking clueless in front of the in-laws. It earned a skim, and the legal section earned a proper read.

journey.quote: What Are the Greek Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
journey.reaction: Reads like a listicle headline. Not a deal-breaker, but it isn't the tone of the rest of the piece, which is calm and grown-up.

journey.quote: It says plainly which belong to the Church and which are simply often told.
journey.reaction: Good. That's an honest framing, not 'magical age-old rituals'. I'd keep reading.

journey.section: Inside the Greek Orthodox wedding service
journey.quote: Tell your photographer and your guests that this, not the rings or a kiss, is the moment to watch.
journey.reaction: Practical, specific, and the sort of thing I'd forward to our photographer. More of this please.

journey.section: How long is a Greek Orthodox wedding service?
journey.quote: Your priest is the right person to ask about timing, since the length depends on the parish, the music and the size of the wedding party.
journey.reaction: You put the question in a heading and then didn't answer it. Even a rough range would help us plan guest transport. This feels like a dodge.

journey.section: Greek wedding traditions from ancient Greece
journey.quote: Encyclopaedias and museum collections describe the ancient customs, including the age at which girls married, in detail.
journey.reaction: So... tell me? This section says the subject exists and then stops. Feels like filler, and the 'age at which girls married' line is an odd thing to dangle without context.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Greece as an Australian
journey.quote: All notarial services are by appointment, though CNI documents can be submitted by post, and CNIs are available for collection within two working days.
journey.reaction: This is the insider-level detail I actually want. Confidence on the legal side is one of our big three, and this reads like someone has done the homework.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Greece as an Australian
journey.quote: Summer brings wildfires and heatwaves from June to September, which is worth weighing if you are set on a midsummer date.
journey.reaction: An honest trade-off. Our grandparents in a heatwave on an island is exactly the worry. I appreciate it being said out loud.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Greece as an Australian
journey.quote: With Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for the plans around the day, from Greece wedding venues to guest travel, and the fee and inclusions are confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Fee and inclusions in writing before committing speaks straight to our hidden-costs fear. One named point of contact answers 'what does end-to-end actually mean' better than most. It's low-key, not a hard sell.

journey.section: Holding a Greek Orthodox wedding in Australia
journey.quote: For a sense of how other couples have brought it together, see a large Greek wedding in Sydney and an Old Hollywood Greek wedding in Melbourne.
journey.reaction: Real weddings are what I'd click next. Would be stronger if the link text told me the venue and year so I knew it was real and recent.

unanswered_questions: Roughly how long does the Orthodox service run, so we can plan guest transport and the reception start time?
If we marry in Greece, how does Wedded Wonderland actually get 40-odd international guests (including grandparents) from the airport to an island venue?
Does the Wedded Advisor work with local Greek planners and suppliers, and are they vetted or just whoever is available?
Who is accountable on the day itself in Greece if something goes wrong?
Can a non-Orthodox partner or koumbaros be accommodated in a church wedding in Greece, and how much lead time does that add?

turn_offs_found.quote: What Are the Greek Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
turn_offs_found.why: Clickbait phrasing. Feels cheaper than the content underneath and is the kind of thing I'd be slightly embarrassed to forward to my parents.

would_share_with: Parents (especially the legal section and the church vs folklore split)

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like to talk through the plans around the day, venues, guest travel and timing, a Wedded Advisor is glad to start that conversation.
cta_reaction.why: Tone is right, no pressure, and the 'fee in writing' line earlier helps. But we're early, haven't picked a destination, and I'd want to read one or two more posts and a real Greek wedding with venue and date before talking to anyone.

top_3_changes: Drop the clickbait title for something calm and confident; the content is better than the headline.
Either give a rough service length or remove the 'How long is a Greek Orthodox wedding service?' heading; flesh out or cut the thin ancient Greece section.
Add one or two lines on how guest travel and on-the-day accountability work for a wedding in Greece, and show venue and year on the real-wedding links.
